items.title: The obstruction to a split injection of finite projective modules being a direct sum of submodules is cut out by a finitely generated ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes finite projective A-modules M, N_1, N_2 and a split injection s : M -> N_1 oplus N_2, and asserts the existence of a finitely generated ideal J of A such that a ring map A -> B factors through A/J exactly when s tensor id_B identifies M tensor B with a direct sum of submodules of N_1 tensor B oplus N_2 tensor B (source lines 28126-28135). The proof chooses a splitting pi, defines the composite projectors p_i = pi o q_i o s with p_1 + p_2 = id_M, and observes that the desired direct-sum condition is equivalent to p_1 and p_2 being orthogonal projectors (proof lines 28138-28142). The real work is then encoding that equivalence as the vanishing of the four endomorphisms p_1 o p_1 - p_1, p_2 o p_2 - p_2, p_1 o p_2 and p_2 o p_1, which forces J to be the smallest ideal containing the entries of those endomorphisms under the identification J tensor End_A(M) (proof lines 28143-28145). The author leaves the remaining details omitted.
